To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sphingosyl phosphocholine (SP-C) and sphingosine are putative regulators for Ca2+ homeostasis in FRTL- 5 cells, and may be of importance for thyroid cell proliferation.
SPC and SP are potent stimulants of intracellular calcium fluxes in rat thyroid cells.
sphingosyl phosphocholine (SP-C) and sphingosine stimulate Ca(2+)(i) in FRTL5 cells via different mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of sphingosines, sphingosine 1-phosphate and ceramide on the proliferation of thyroid cells.
the effect of sphingosines and their derivatives on calcium flux in thyroid FRTL5 cells.
the effects of SPC and SP on Ca2+ homeostasis in FRTL- 5 cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sphingosines and their derivatives are involved in the regulation of thyroid function and growth.
the sphingosine derivative, SPC, is a potent activator of the Ca(2+ )influx in thyroid FRTL 5 cells.
SPC and SP may act as putative second messengers in FRTL- 5 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sphingosyl phosphocholine is a putative regulator of Ca2+ influx in thyroid cells.

the SPC-evokes increase of intracellular free Ca(2+) is mediated by activation of a pertussis toxin-sensitive G-protein coupled to phospholipase C and subsequent formation of inositol trisphosphate, whereas the SP-evoked increase of intracellular Ca(2+) may be mediated by activation of phospholipase A(2) with subsequent formation of diacylglycerol and arachidonic acid.
sphingosyl derivatives may act as second messengers in FRTL- 5 cells, and may be important in modulating thyroid cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sphingosyl derivatives are important regulators of Ca2+.
SPC and SP are putative regulators for Ca2+ flux in FRTL- 5 cells, and SP and SPC act on Ca2+ via different mechanisms.
Sphingosylphosphate and Sphingosine are both involved in Ca2+ flux regulation in FRTL- cells.
